balanced_fit#

class imbal.classification.balanced_fit(model, x=None, y=None, class_weights=None, sample_weights=None, compile_parameters=None, validation_data=None, epochs=1, batch_size=32, shuffle=True, stratify_batches=True, generate_decoder_branch=False, representation_layer_index=-3, **kwargs)#

Bases:

Performs a class-balanced fit, where each class is equally weighted during the model fitting process.

Includes the ability to optionally generate a decoder branch extending from the provided model, which aids in achieving a better representation space, usually resulting in better performance on imbalanced data. This feature, enabled using generate_decoder_branch, is off by default due to its experimental nature, but we recommend using it if your model fits the anticipated structure (see imbal.util.backend.generate_decoder_branch for more details).

Parameters:

  • model – The model to perform the decoupled fit on.

  • x – Optional, default None (Same as model.fit). A NumPy array of data points, arranged as a column vector

  • y –

    Optional, default None (Same as model.fit). A NumPy array of labels, arranged as a row vector, column vector, or list of one-hot vectors.

  • class_weights – Optional, default None. A list of class weights, or a dictionary mapping class labels to class weights.

  • sample_weights – Optional, default None. A list of sample weights. If specified, overrides class_weights.

  • compile_parameters – Optional, default None. A TFModelCompileParameters object, or a dictionary mapping Tensorflow model.compile parameters to their corresponding values. If set to None, the default model.compile parameters will be used.

  • validation_data –

    Optional, default None (Same as model.fit). The data used to validate the model during training. See Tensorflow’s model.fit documentation.

  • epochs –

    Optional, default 1 (Same as model.fit). The number of epochs to train for. If an int, the provided number of epochs will be used during the first stage, and halved for the second stage. If a tuple or list of length 2, the value in the first index will be used as the number of epochs in the first stage of training, and the second index for the number of epochs in the second stage of training.

  • batch_size –

    Optional, default None (Same as model.fit). The batch size to use during training.

  • shuffle –

    Optional, default True (Same as model.fit). Whether to shuffle the data before each epoch.

  • stratify_batches – Optional, default True. Whether to stratify data batch-wise during training. See DatasetWithBatching for details. Only used when multi_output is True.

  • generate_decoder_branch – Optional, default False. When set to True, an extended version of the provided model containing a decoder branch is generated and used for training, often yielding better training results (see Comparison of Fit Methods). Decoder generation is experimental and may not always be possible depending on model structure.

  • representation_layer_index – Optional, default -3. Used only when generate_decoder_branch is True. The index of the layer from which the decoder branch in generated. It is recommended that this layer is no later than the third to last layer of the model, to help ensure that the remaining layers in the classifier portion of the model may allow for non-linear relationships to be learned.

Returns:

None

Example:

>>> # Assume MNIST data is already loaded in '(x_train, y_train), (x_test, y_test)'
>>> # and that a model is already created in 'model'

>>> import imbal
>>> import keras

>>> parameters = imbal.classification.compile_parameters(
>>>     loss="categorical_crossentropy",
>>>     optimizer=keras.optimizers.Adam(),
>>>     metrics=["accuracy"]
>>> )

>>> imbal.classification.balanced_fit(
>>>     model,
>>>     x_train,
>>>     y_train,
>>>     compile_parameters=parameters,
>>>     epochs=10,
>>>     batch_size=512
>>> )
